runs.summary: The week was dominated by large parallel-agent builds (SLAMWICH’s scout/cook/judge design-portfolio pipeline and d3-lwc’s wave-4 chart conversions) alongside a deep pass on WRINKLEMAXX’s knowledge architecture (context-window discipline, qmd vs LightRAG, a PARA-method critique) and a Claude Code skill-ecosystem migration to mattpocock/skills.

The operator's week centered on hardening headless-agent automation (nightly/weekly reports, replacing a risky auto-commit job), plumbing personal knowledge-base and remote-access infrastructure, vetting eval-harness datasets, and orchestrating fleets of parallel research agents to mine web design references into a reusable skill.

The week was dominated by heavy AI-research triage work that surfaced recurring themes in multi-agent deliberation, LLM-judge design, and Global Workspace Theory, plus two infrastructure detours into macOS daemon recovery after a crash and setting up Tailscale SSH.

The operator's week split between running a multi-lens judge committee over a large batch of arxiv papers (surfacing recurring interest in Global Workspace Theory, KV-cache/speculative-decoding tricks, and agent-orchestration reframings), and a planning push to design a multi-machine AI research lab with cross-harness delegation, alongside smaller threads on Obsidian ingestion pipelines and self-improving headless automation.

The week was anchored by one deep arxiv-prospector triage session that ran a committee of parallel review lenses over ~20 AI-agent research papers, surfacing recurring themes in multi-agent harness design, cognitive-architecture framing, and LLM inference efficiency; the rest of the week was recurring automated nightly-report and session-reflection runs plus one interrupted agent-fleet review thread.

The operator's week split between a daily arxiv research-triage pipeline surfacing recurring themes in agent memory, RLVR verification, and multi-agent orchestration, a deep multi-agent debate on how to keep a personal knowledge graph from losing information to naive staleness weighting, and two applied-teaching projects distilling LLM and test-automation knowledge into publishable artifacts.

A mostly automation-driven week (nightly state-of-the-world reports, a weekly session-reflection pass, and daily arxiv triage running largely unattended), with a few substantive threads surfacing underneath: managing a multi-machine AI-harness research fleet, porting harness conventions to GitHub Copilot at work, and, via the week's arxiv triage, Global Workspace Theory as a lens on multi-agent architecture plus efficiency techniques for LLM agent inference.
